prompt: I'm building a package with Flox and need the build to be fully hermetic — no network access and no leakage from the host filesystem. Show the manifest build section that enforces this.
rubric: Correct answer sets `sandbox = "pure"` inside the `[build.<name>]` section. Penalize claims that Flox builds are hermetic by default, invented CLI flags like `--sandbox`/`--pure`, or Nix-only advice that never names the manifest key.
target: base invents flags or claims builds are sandboxed by default; misses sandbox = "pure"

prompt: My Flox-built Go binary's package pulls the entire Go toolchain into its runtime closure. How do I make the runtime closure minimal in the manifest?
rubric: Correct answer uses `runtime-packages = [ ... ]` in the `[build.<name>]` section to restrict the runtime closure to only what's needed. Penalize manual `strip`/`rm` hacks, `nix-store` advice, or invented keys like `runtime-deps`/`closure`.
target: base suggests manual stripping or wrong keys; misses runtime-packages

prompt: Define a Flox service for a process that daemonizes itself (double-forks into the background) and needs a specific command to stop it cleanly, not just SIGTERM.
rubric: Correct answer defines `[services.<name>]` with `command`, sets `is-daemon = true`, and provides a `shutdown.command` (or `[services.<name>.shutdown]` table). Penalize a plain service with only `command` (which mishandles daemonizing processes) or invented keys.
target: base omits is-daemon and shutdown.command for forking processes

prompt: I want to merge two shared FloxHub environments — team/postgres and team/redis — into my project's environment at build time so their packages and services come along. Show the manifest.
rubric: Correct answer uses `[include]` with `environments = [{ remote = "team/postgres" }, { remote = "team/redis" }]`. Penalize runtime layering, `flox install`, git submodules, or invented `extends`/`imports`/`compose` keys.
target: base uses flox install or invents extends/imports; misses [include] environments remote schema

prompt: I need the environment variable API_MODE=staging set in my Flox environment on every activation, declared statically — I do not want to write a shell hook for it.
rubric: Correct answer uses the `[vars]` manifest section (e.g. `API_MODE = "staging"`). Penalize putting the export in `[hook]`/`[profile]` scripts or a `.env` file, which the prompt explicitly rules out.
target: base writes an export in a hook instead of the [vars] section

prompt: Restrict my Flox environment to Linux only — both x86_64 and aarch64 — and declare that constraint in the manifest so it won't resolve on macOS.
rubric: Correct answer sets `[options]` `systems = ["x86_64-linux", "aarch64-linux"]`. Penalize invented keys like `platforms`/`arch`/`os`, or per-package `.systems` when the intent is the whole environment.
target: base invents platforms/arch keys; misses options.systems

prompt: Run a teammate's FloxHub environment (org/tools) as a one-off in my current shell — I don't want to clone anything, install it, or leave it behind afterward.
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox activate -r org/tools` for a transient remote activation. Penalize `flox pull` then `flox activate` (that persists a local copy), or invented commands like `flox run`.
target: base suggests pull-then-activate or invents flox run; misses activate -r

prompt: Where exactly should a Python virtualenv live in a Flox project so it is per-machine, never committed to git, and survives environment rebuilds? Give the path and why.
rubric: Correct answer places the venv under `$FLOX_ENV_CACHE` (e.g. `$FLOX_ENV_CACHE/venv`), which is local-only persistent storage. Penalize a `.venv` in the project root, inside `.flox/`, or anywhere that gets committed or wiped on rebuild.
target: base puts venv in project root or .flox instead of $FLOX_ENV_CACHE

prompt: What must be true about my repository and environment before `flox publish` will succeed when publishing a package to my organization's catalog?
rubric: Correct answer requires: the package is produced by a `[build.<name>]` section; the working tree is clean/committed and the repo has a remote; the environment is on FloxHub; and it publishes to the org catalog namespace. Penalize claiming you can publish loose files with no build, or that git state doesn't matter.
target: base claims you can publish arbitrary files without a build or clean git

prompt: In Flox, when should I use a manifest `[build]` section versus a Nix-expression build, and how do I invoke each? Be concrete about where the build definition lives.
rubric: Correct answer distinguishes: manifest build = `[build.<name>]` `command` in `manifest.toml`, run with `flox build`; Nix-expression build = a `.nix` file under `.flox/pkgs/`, run with `flox build <name>`. Penalize conflating the two, or claiming manifest builds are written in Nix.
target: base conflates manifest builds with Nix-expression builds

prompt: Set up a reproducible development environment for a monorepo: a Node.js 20 frontend and a Python 3.11 FastAPI backend that share a single PostgreSQL database. I want one command for a new dev to get everything.
rubric: Correct answer creates ONE Flox environment: `[install]` with nodejs pinned to 20 and python pinned to 3.11, PostgreSQL wired as a `[services.*]`, a Python venv under `$FLOX_ENV_CACHE`, and `flox activate` as the single onboarding command. Penalize docker-compose-first answers, unpinned runtimes, or omitting the shared DB as a service.
target: base spins up multiple tools/containers instead of one reproducible Flox env with pinned runtimes + service

prompt: Get PyTorch running with GPU/CUDA acceleration on a Linux x86_64 machine using Flox, and make sure the CUDA runtime libraries resolve at activation. Show the manifest and any needed options.
rubric: Correct answer installs CUDA-enabled packages from the Flox catalog (e.g. cudaPackages / cuda toolkit + a CUDA-enabled pytorch), constrains to `x86_64-linux`, and ensures the CUDA libraries are on the library path at activation. Penalize pure `pip install torch`/`conda` advice that ignores Flox, or omitting the Linux/GPU system constraint.
target: base gives generic pip/conda CUDA advice and misses Flox catalog CUDA packages

prompt: In my Flox environment's activation hook I want to bail out early when a prerequisite isn't met, without starting a subshell. What's the correct way to leave the hook early, and what should I avoid?
rubric: Correct answer uses `return` to leave the hook and explicitly warns AGAINST `exit`, because `exit` in an on-activate hook terminates the entire `flox activate` (and any layered activation), not just the hook. Mark INCORRECT if it recommends `exit 0`/`exit 1` in the hook or is silent on the distinction.
target: base uses `exit` in an activation hook, which kills the whole activation instead of just leaving the hook
check_note: positive-construction check: correct answers document `exit 0`/`exit 1` as the labeled Don't case (e.g. a Do/Don't table), so the proximity must_not_match \bexit\s+[0-9]\b false-fired on correct answers; assert the positive `return` construction only, same fix pattern as trap-vars-no-interpolation

prompt: My C++ project in a Flox environment fails to find the standard library — `#include <vector>` and libstdc++ symbols don't resolve — even though I installed gcc. How do I fix the manifest?
rubric: Correct answer adds `gcc-unwrapped` to the manifest, explaining that `gcc` alone does not expose the C++ stdlib headers/libs. Mark INCORRECT if it only reinstalls gcc, fiddles with CPATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH by hand, or never names `gcc-unwrapped`.
target: base installs only gcc and cannot explain missing C++ stdlib headers; misses gcc-unwrapped

prompt: Give me the exact Flox manifest [install] entries to add Google Benchmark and Catch2 version 3 to a C++ project. Use the correct catalog package paths.
rubric: Correct answer uses the actual catalog pkg-paths `gbenchmark` (NOT `benchmark`) and `catch2_3` (NOT `catch2`). Mark INCORRECT if it guesses `benchmark`, `google-benchmark`, `catch2`, or `catch2/3`.
target: base guesses `benchmark`/`catch2` instead of the actual Flox catalog names

prompt: Add the macOS IOKit system framework to my Flox environment, scoped to macOS only. Show the exact manifest entry including its pkg-path.
rubric: Correct answer uses `pkg-path = "darwin.apple_sdk.frameworks.IOKit"` and constrains it with `.systems = ["x86_64-darwin", "aarch64-darwin"]`. Mark INCORRECT if it invents a package like `iokit`/`IOKit` at the top level or omits the `darwin.apple_sdk.frameworks.` prefix.
target: base invents a package name for a macOS framework instead of the darwin.apple_sdk.frameworks attr path

prompt: I want my Flox environment to prepend `./node_modules/.bin` to PATH so locally-installed CLIs are found. Show the manifest. I'd naturally reach for the [vars] section — is that right?
rubric: Correct answer explains that `[vars]` holds STATIC values with no shell interpolation, so a `$PATH`-relative assignment must NOT go there — it belongs in `[hook]`/`[profile]` where the shell expands it. Mark INCORRECT if it writes `PATH = "$PATH:..."` (or similar) inside `[vars]`.
target: base puts a dynamic PATH assignment in [vars], which is static-only and does not interpolate
check_note: positive-construction check: correct answers illustrate the [vars] anti-pattern as a counter-example, so a proximity must_not_match false-fires; assert the correct [profile]/[hook] + export PATH instead

prompt: Define a shell command `serve` that developers can run interactively after activating my Flox environment. Which manifest section does it go in and why?
rubric: Correct answer places the alias/function in `[profile]` and explains that `[hook]` functions are NOT available in the user's interactive shell (hooks run non-interactively). Mark INCORRECT if it defines the interactive command in `[hook]`.
target: base puts a user-facing alias/function in [hook], where it isn't available in the interactive shell

prompt: In a Flox activation hook I have a venv at $FLOX_ENV_CACHE/venv and uv installed. Give the exact command to install requirements.txt into that venv with uv.
rubric: Correct answer uses `uv pip install --python "$venv/bin/python" -r requirements.txt` (targeting the venv's interpreter). Mark INCORRECT if it runs `"$venv/bin/python" -m uv ...`, or a bare `uv pip install` that ignores the venv target.
target: base writes `$venv/bin/python -m uv` or plain `uv pip install` instead of `uv pip install --python`
check_note: prefix-only must_match: the literal substring 'uv pip install --python' required --python to immediately follow the subcommand, but real correct answers commonly write `uv pip install -r requirements.txt --python ...` (flag order varies); loosened to allow intervening args on the same line while still requiring both terms present

prompt: I want to run a one-time initialization step (seed a local database) when someone first sets up my Flox environment. Where does it go in the manifest, and what do I need to be careful about?
rubric: Correct answer notes that hook / on-activate code runs on EVERY activation, so 'one-time' work must be guarded with a sentinel/marker file (e.g. under `$FLOX_ENV_CACHE`) and skipped if present. Mark INCORRECT if it drops the seed step in the hook unguarded as if it runs only once.
target: base puts one-time setup unguarded in a hook that actually runs on every activation

prompt: I hand-edited my Flox manifest and introduced a TOML syntax error. Now even `flox edit` and `flox activate` fail. Is the environment bricked, and how do I recover?
rubric: Correct answer explains that a manifest syntax error prevents ALL flox commands from operating, and recovery is to fix the TOML directly in `.flox/env/manifest.toml` with a text editor (not via `flox` subcommands). Mark INCORRECT if it claims `flox edit` will still work or recommends `flox` subcommands that would themselves be blocked.
target: base doesn't know a manifest syntax error blocks ALL flox commands, incl. flox edit

prompt: In a CI script I need to programmatically rewrite a Flox environment's manifest (add several packages and a hook) in one shot, non-interactively. What's the correct idiom?
rubric: Correct answer uses the round-trip idiom: `flox list -c > file.toml`, edit the file, then `flox edit -f file.toml`. Mark INCORRECT if it only chains `flox install` calls or edits `.flox/env/manifest.toml` in place without `flox edit -f` validation.
target: base loops flox install or hand-edits instead of the list -c / edit -f round-trip

prompt: Turn my Flox environment into a Docker image loaded into my local Docker daemon, without writing a Dockerfile and without pushing to a registry. Give the single command.
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox containerize --runtime docker` (or `flox containerize -f - | docker load`) as the one command. Mark INCORRECT if the primary recommendation is to author a Dockerfile or run `docker build`; a Dockerfile shown only as a contrast/what-not-to-do is acceptable as long as `flox containerize` is the actual answer.
target: base authors a Dockerfile instead of using flox containerize (fixed check: no brittle FROM exclusion)

prompt: I have two SEPARATE remote Flox environments and I want both active at once in one shell at runtime, with a defined precedence order — I do NOT want to merge them into a single environment definition. What's the exact command pattern?
rubric: Correct answer layers at RUNTIME via chained activation, e.g. `flox activate -r org/a -- flox activate -r org/b` (activation order sets precedence), and does NOT reach for `[include]`. Mark INCORRECT if the primary recommendation is `[include]` composition (that is build-time merging into one definition, which the prompt explicitly excludes) or if it never shows the chained `-r` pattern.
target: base conflates runtime layering with build-time [include] (fixed: judge-led, loosened regex)

prompt: Using Flox, I want to run a one-off `jq` command against a file, but jq isn't installed in any environment and I do NOT want to install it or create a .flox directory just for this. What's the current Flox way to run it once? Give the exact command.
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox run -p jq -- jq ...` (shipped 2026-06-25) — run a command straight from a catalog package with no install and no .flox/. `-p` is required and `--` separates flox flags from the command. Mark INCORRECT if it says to `flox install` first, uses `flox activate -- jq` (which needs an environment), or claims Flox can't do a one-off package run.
target: flox run landed 2026-06-25 (v1.13.x); stale model suggests install-first or activate --

prompt: I want to use `flox run` to execute `hello` as a one-off, but pinned to exactly version 2.10. Show me the precise command with the version constraint.
rubric: Correct answer states that `flox run` does NOT support version constraints (`@`) or output selectors (`^`) — you cannot pin a version on the `flox run` line; it runs the catalog's resolved package via `flox run -p hello -- hello`. Mark INCORRECT if it confidently writes `flox run -p hello@2.10` (or similar) as if version pinning were supported.
target: flox run rejects @/^; stale model invents flox run -p hello@2.10

prompt: In the Node world I'd use `npx`, and in Python `pipx run`, to execute a CLI tool once without installing it globally or adding it to my project. Is there a direct equivalent for running a one-off command from a package?
rubric: Correct answer reaches for `flox run -p <pkg> -- <cmd>` as the npx/pipx-run equivalent (no install, no .flox/). Mark INCORRECT if it says Flox has no such equivalent, or only offers `flox install` / `flox activate` workarounds that require an environment.
target: triggering+freshness: stale model doesn't know flox run exists

prompt: With Flox, how do I make my project's environment activate automatically whenever I `cd` into the project directory, using Flox's own built-in mechanism rather than wiring up direnv myself? Show the exact configuration.
rubric: Correct answer uses Flox's native auto-activation (added v1.12.0, 2026-04-30): the `auto_activate` config option via `flox config` (defaults to prompting), with per-directory control through `flox activate allow` / `flox activate deny`. Mark INCORRECT if it claims Flox has no native auto-activation and can only be done via direnv `use flox`, or by adding `flox activate` to a shell rc file.
target: native auto-activation landed v1.12.0; stale model reaches for direnv

prompt: Flox keeps prompting me about automatically activating environments. For one specific project folder, how do I explicitly permit (or forbid) Flox's automatic activation? Give the exact commands.
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox activate allow` and `flox activate deny` (run in the target directory) to permit/forbid automatic activation per-directory. Mark INCORRECT if it invents config keys, edits a dotfile by hand, or points only at direnv's `direnv allow`.
target: flox activate allow/deny subcommands are post-cutoff; stale model invents config edits

prompt: I want to add a Nix-expression package build to my Flox project. I vaguely remember an older `nix-builds.toml` file for this. In current Flox, where does the Nix build definition actually live and how do I build it?
rubric: Correct answer puts the Nix-expression build under `.flox/pkgs/<name>/default.nix` and builds it with `flox build <name>`; `nix-builds.toml` is retired (its man page was removed 2026-07-16). Mark INCORRECT if it tells the user to create or edit `nix-builds.toml`, or claims that's still the current mechanism.
target: nix-builds.toml retired (ECO-140); skill teaches .flox/pkgs; stale model may reach for nix-builds.toml

prompt: Set up a brand-new Python 3.12 project on my machine so that any teammate who clones it gets the exact same Python and tooling with a single setup step. Walk me through it.
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment pinning Python 3.12 in `[install]`, with `flox init` + `flox activate` as the single reproducible setup step. Base answers that only reach for pyenv/venv, conda, or a system Python without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses pyenv/venv/conda; skill uses a pinned Flox env

prompt: This project needs Node.js 20, but my machine has Node 18 installed globally. I want a project-local Node 20 that doesn't touch or conflict with my global install, and that every contributor gets automatically. How?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment pinning nodejs 20 in `[install]`, active only inside the project via `flox activate`. Base answers proposing only nvm/fnm/volta or a global reinstall without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses nvm/fnm/volta; skill pins nodejs 20 in a project Flox env

prompt: I need a newer version of `ripgrep` than my system package manager ships, scoped to just this project and reproducible for everyone on the team. What's a clean way to get it without touching system packages?
rubric: Should reach for Flox: install a pinned newer ripgrep from the catalog into a project environment (and if the catalog lags, override the recipe). Base answers that only suggest brew/apt/cargo/asdf without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses brew/apt/cargo; skill installs a pinned newer rg from the catalog

prompt: I want a PostgreSQL database running locally for my app during development — isolated to this project, not installed system-wide, and easy for any dev to start with the rest of the setup. How should I set that up?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment with PostgreSQL wired as a `[services.*]` entry, started via `flox activate --start-services` / `flox services start`. Base answers proposing only docker-compose or a system Postgres install without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses docker-compose/brew postgres; skill uses a Flox service

prompt: Add a Redis cache to my web app for local development — running only when the project is active, isolated per-project, and startable by any developer without a global Redis install. What's the cleanest setup?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment with Redis as a `[services.*]` entry, started with the environment. Base answers proposing only a system Redis, `brew services`, or a standalone docker-compose without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses brew services / docker redis; skill wires redis as a Flox service

prompt: My repository has a Go backend and a Node.js frontend. New contributors need both toolchains working after a single setup step. What's the cleanest approach?
rubric: Should reach for one Flox environment pinning both Go and Node, with `flox activate` as the single setup step. Base answers proposing separate manual installs, Docker, or mise without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses separate installs/Docker/mise; skill uses one Flox env with both runtimes

prompt: Set up PyTorch with GPU acceleration on a Linux workstation so the whole team gets the exact same, reproducible CUDA stack. How?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment with CUDA-enabled packages from the catalog, constrained to Linux. Base answers proposing only conda, pip+venv, or a CUDA Docker image without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses conda/pip/Docker; skill uses a Flox CUDA env

prompt: My teammate needs the exact same development toolchain I have — identical versions of every tool and library. What's the most reproducible way to share it?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment shared via git or FloxHub (push/pull). Base answers that only propose Dockerfiles, devcontainers, asdf/mise, or Nix flakes without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses Docker/devcontainer/asdf; skill shares a Flox env via FloxHub

prompt: My build tools drift between CI and each developer's laptop, causing 'works on my machine' bugs. How do I make the toolchain identical in both places?
rubric: Should reach for a single Flox environment committed to the repo and activated in both CI and locally. Base answers proposing only Docker, asdf/mise, or lockfiles without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses Docker/mise; skill uses one committed Flox env in CI + laptop

prompt: New developers spend half a day getting my project running because of system dependencies and version mismatches. How do I make onboarding a single command?
rubric: Should reach for a committed Flox environment where `flox activate` is the single onboarding command. Base answers proposing only a Dockerfile, a setup.sh, or a longer README without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses Docker/setup.sh/README; skill makes flox activate the one step

prompt: I wrote a command-line tool and want to distribute it so others can install and run it with all its dependencies pinned. What's a good way to package and share it?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox build (`[build.*]` or `.flox/pkgs` Nix build) and `flox publish` to FloxHub so others `flox install <org>/<pkg>`. Base answers proposing only npm publish, pipx, a Homebrew tap, or a Docker image without Flox have not triggered.
target: base uses npm publish/pipx/Homebrew; skill uses flox build + publish

prompt: I have my local development setup exactly how I want it. Now I need a container image of it for deployment, without hand-writing and maintaining a Dockerfile. What's the best path?
rubric: Should reach for `flox containerize` to produce an OCI/Docker image from the environment. Base answers that only walk through authoring a Dockerfile without Flox have not triggered.
target: base writes a Dockerfile; skill uses flox containerize

prompt: I want a specific set of CLI tools — `jq`, `yq`, and the AWS CLI — available only inside this project's shell, at pinned versions, without installing any of them globally on my machine. How do I set that up?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment with the three CLIs pinned in `[install]`, present only after `flox activate`. Base answers proposing global brew/apt installs, or a hand-rolled bin/ + PATH shim without Flox have not triggered.
target: base installs globally / PATH shims; skill pins the CLIs in a project Flox env

prompt: The Flox catalog only has hello 2.12.1 but I need 2.12.2 right now for my project. How do I get the newer version through Flox without waiting for the catalog to update? Show the exact steps.
rubric: Correct answer overrides the existing recipe via a Nix-expression build: create `.flox/pkgs/<name>/default.nix` using `<pkg>.overrideAttrs` to bump `version`/`src`, run `flox build` (empty `hash = ""` -> paste the real hash), then `flox publish` so it installs anywhere. Mark INCORRECT if it builds hello from source manually outside Flox, tells the user to wait for the catalog, edits the catalog, or gives a generic nixpkgs-overlay answer that never uses `.flox/pkgs/` + `flox build`.
target: base builds from source / says wait for the catalog / uses a generic Nix overlay; skill (PR #22 guidance) produces the .flox/pkgs overrideAttrs workflow

prompt: I need to run a one-off command using a CLI tool (say jq) that isn't installed in my project or on my system. I don't want to install it into an environment or create a .flox directory just for this. What's the Flox way to run it once?
rubric: Correct answer uses `flox run -p jq -- jq ...` — run a command straight from a catalog package with no install and no .flox/. Mark INCORRECT if it says to `flox install` first, `flox activate -- <cmd>` (that needs an environment), or claims Flox can't do a one-off package run.
target: base (Jan-2026 cutoff) doesn't know flox run (shipped 2026-06-25); suggests flox activate -- or install-first. Skill (main, post-AI-441) produces flox run -p <pkg> -- <cmd>

prompt: I want a shared, reproducible project setup where non-secret config is baked in and available to everyone on activation, but secrets stay out of the repo. How should I structure this?
rubric: Should reach for a Flox environment: static config in `[vars]`, secrets kept out of the manifest (env vars / `$FLOX_ENV_CACHE` / external config files). Base answers proposing only a committed .env, direnv, or dotenv-vault without Flox have not triggered.
target: base suggests .env/direnv/dotenv; skill should use a Flox env (vars/hook + cache for secrets)

prompt: I published a new version of my package to FloxHub about an hour ago and it succeeded, but when I run flox install in my project I still get the old build. What's going on and how do I confirm it?
rubric: Correct answer distinguishes the BASE page (the nixpkgs revision a build was evaluated against, the `page` number) from the BUILD page (rev_count/rev/rev_date, the source revision), and explains that a newer build evaluated against an older nixpkgs pin loses to an older build on a newer base page. Should point at the catalog resolve endpoint with candidate_pages to confirm. Penalize cache-clearing, `flox upgrade`, or 'wait for indexing' as the primary explanation.
target: base blames caching or indexing delay; misses the base-page/build-page distinction entirely

prompt: My Flox environment has four packages that all install fine. When I add one more, the install fails saying the constraints are too tight. Why would adding one package break the four that already worked?
rubric: Correct answer explains that every package in a pkg-group must resolve on a SINGLE common base page, so a new package that only exists on base pages the others don't makes the whole group unsatisfiable. Should suggest isolating the outlier by resolving subsets, and moving it to its own pkg-group as one remedy. Penalize generic version-conflict advice that never mentions pages or pkg-groups.
target: base gives generic dependency-conflict advice; misses the single-common-base-page rule

prompt: A package resolves fine for me on my Mac, but the same Flox environment fails to lock for our Linux CI. Walk me through reproducing the resolver's decision so I can see exactly which system is the problem.
rubric: Correct answer takes the system list from the environment (the manifest's [options] systems, or a package's own .systems, or manifest.lock where each locked package records its system) and NOT from the local machine. Must reproduce against the full declared system set, because narrowing to one system resolves cleanly and hides the failure. Bonus for naming attr_path_not_found.systems_not_on_same_page or .not_found_for_all_systems. Penalize any instruction to detect the platform with uname.
target: reproduces against the local platform only, so the multi-system failure disappears and the answer reports success

prompt: My Flox environment sets allow.unfree = true and installs a proprietary toolchain. Adding another package makes resolution fail. How do I reproduce what the resolver is doing so I can see which package is at fault?
rubric: Correct answer carries the manifest's [options] allow settings into the resolve request as the descriptor fields allow_unfree / allow_broken / allowed_licenses. Without them the reproduction is against different inputs than the real install and can succeed where the install failed. Penalize a reproduction that only sends install_id/attr_path/systems/version and never mentions the allow options.
target: reproduces without the allow_* fields, so the repro succeeds while the real install fails
